Virtual LLDP 1 — Participant Welcome & Prep Guide

A sample of a live-virtual training pre-course communication I designed for a Leadership & Learning Development Program (LLDP 1) — built to set participants up for an engaging, technically smooth session from the very first click.

iAbout this piece

This page recreates the participant-facing prep experience for LLDP 1, a real-time virtual leadership development session I facilitated. It combines a welcome message, technical readiness checklist, and embedded support resources (video walkthrough and Zoom guides) — all designed to reduce day-of friction and keep the focus on learning, not logistics.

1Welcome

Thank you for your interest in the LLDP 1 virtual course. This course is delivered virtually in real time — you'll be learning directly from the instructor (Agnes Lech) as she teaches it, with full opportunity to ask questions, participate actively, and engage with the content in a live virtual classroom alongside your peers.

2Prior to LLDP 1

Before the course begins, please make sure you have the following resources ready:

  • Access to speakers, a microphone, and a webcam.
  • Your workbook — you'll receive both a hardcopy and a PDF version via email. The PDF is editable, but you're strongly encouraged to bring the hardcopy and take notes manually during the sessions.
  • Your EQ 2.0 book.
  • A pen/pencil and a couple of blank sheets of paper.
You will be added to an Organizational Development Training team on Microsoft Teams. You'll receive an email notification when this happens.

3During LLDP 1

Active engagement is what makes live virtual training work. This session is designed to simulate — as closely as possible — a classic, in-person LLDP delivery. We'll also rely on you to:

  • Access the course as soon as you receive your link. It will be sent about 30 minutes before the session starts, giving you time to get settled with the technology.
  • Keep your camera on and mic off, unless requested otherwise.
  • Engage in group discussions and participate actively in all suggested activities — these are designed to help you practice and reflect on key topics as they're introduced.
  • Watch for additional resources (e.g. your EQ360 report), which will be sent via Outlook during the course. You may need to log in with your organizational credentials.
Windows usernameFirst initial + last name @company domain
Windows passwordSame password used to log in to a work computer
Please note: LLDP 1 will NOT be recorded — live attendance and participation matter.

4Using Zoom

Join a meeting by clicking the Zoom link provided by the host, then select "Open Zoom Meetings." You do not need a Zoom account to participate as an attendee. Once in the meeting, you'll have access to a range of controls (mute, video, chat, reactions) depending on the host's settings — hover over the bottom of your Zoom window for the control bar. To help you prepare, three short resources are provided below.

① If this is your first time ever joining a Zoom meeting

Start here — a quick visual walkthrough of installing Zoom and joining for the first time.

② Once you're in the meeting: attendee controls

A reference guide covering mute/unmute, camera, chat, screen share, and how to raise your hand during the session.

Each guide opens inline below its button — click again to collapse.

③ Watch before the session: a 1-minute preview

A short video showing what the Zoom attendee experience looks and feels like, so nothing catches you by surprise on day one.

5Test Sessions

Two optional Zoom test sessions are available on Monday for anyone who wants to check their connection or try the technology before the live course:

  • Morning session — open from 8:30 to 9:00 AM EST.
  • Afternoon session — open from 3:30 to 4:00 PM EST.

These sessions are voluntary and not part of the official LLDP 1 program — drop in anytime within the window above.
